bib.title: Know What You Don’t Know: Unanswerable Questions for SQuAD
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 56th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Short Papers)

read.skipped: Appendices A.1 and A.2 are referenced but not in the PDF

question: Can a reading comprehension dataset with adversarially written unanswerable questions force extractive models to know when no answer is supported?
hypothesis: Crowdworker-written unanswerable questions with plausible answers are harder than automatically generated negatives and expose a large human-machine gap.
contributions: SQuAD 2.0 (SQuADRUn): SQuAD plus 53,775 adversarial unanswerable questions
Analysis of negative-example types and human accuracy
Comparison against TFIDF and RULEBASED automatic negatives

method.summary: Crowdworkers wrote unanswerable questions for SQuAD paragraphs that look relevant and have a plausible answer span; the result was merged with SQuAD splits. Three existing no-answer models were trained and tested, with an abstention threshold tuned on dev.
method.task: extractive reading comprehension with unanswerable questions

datasets.name: SQuADRUn (SQuAD 2.0)
datasets.size: train 130,319 (43,498 negative); dev 11,873 (5,945 negative); test 8,862 (4,332 negative)
datasets.source: SQuAD plus 53,775 crowdworker-written unanswerable questions (Daemo); CC BY-SA 4.0
datasets.preprocessing: Removed questions from workers who wrote 25 or fewer questions on an article, applied to new and existing SQuAD questions; dev/test articles without collected unanswerable questions removed

datasets.name: SQuAD + TFIDF
datasets.split: train negatives only for the 285 articles with SQuADRUn negatives; test on SQuADRUn dev articles with roughly 1:1 negatives
datasets.source: Clark and Gardner (2017) TF-IDF paragraph pairing

models.name: BiDAF-No-Answer (BNA)
models.architecture: BiDAF with no-answer probability (Levy et al. 2017)

training.objective: inferred: answer span distribution plus predicted probability that the question is unanswerable

other.note: hyperparameters not given; code on Codalab

inference.decoding: abstain when predicted unanswerable probability exceeds a threshold

parameters.threshold: tuned per model on dev; test uses the threshold maximizing dev F1

metrics.name: Exact Match
metrics.definition: average EM following Rajpurkar et al. 2016; for negative examples abstaining scores 1, any other response 0

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: average token F1; abstaining on negatives scores 1, else 0

eval.protocol: Human accuracy: extra crowdworkers answered all dev and test questions, 4.8 answers per question on average, majority vote with ties favouring answering and shorter answers. Single run per model; no seeds or significance test stated.

availability.data: released as SQuAD 2.0 on the SQuAD leaderboard, CC BY-SA 4.0
